case.court_name: Court of Appeal of Sri Lanka
case.source_citation: CA 169/2003, High Court Gampaha 48/94, decided 16 June 2008

clause.text: Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the procedural irregularities at the retrial affected the legality of punishment imposed and the fairness of the trial under Article 13(4).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The accused-appellant argued that the irregularities in the retrial process violated his fundamental rights including the right to be punished only by a competent court.
case_context.respondent_argument: The Attorney-General argued that the irregularities were procedural and did not affect the legality of the punishment or the trial's fairness.
key_facts: The accused was sentenced to death at the retrial.
The retrial failed to comply with mandatory procedural requirements.
The accused had already undergone eight years of incarceration.
The court considered whether the irregularities amounted to a failure of justice.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 13(4) as ensuring that punishment can only be imposed by a competent court following a fair trial. The failure to comply with mandatory procedural safeguards at the retrial meant the court was not competent to impose punishment.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Because the retrial was procedurally flawed, the conviction and death sentence were invalid under Article 13(4). The court also noted that detention before trial is not punishment, and the accused had already served significant detention.
principles_established: Punishment must be imposed only by a competent court after a fair trial.
Procedural irregularities that violate fair trial rights undermine the court's competence to punish.
Detention before trial is not punishment.

outcome.holding: The conviction and death sentence were set aside due to failure to comply with procedural safeguards, invalidating the punishment under Article 13(4).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Conviction and sentence set aside; accused acquitted.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(4) was materially engaged to emphasize that punishment can only be imposed by a competent court after a fair trial, which was not the case here due to procedural failures at the retrial.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court held that punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and that the failure to comply with mandatory procedural provisions at the retrial occasioned a failure of justice, invalidating the conviction and sentence.
